result.headline: Pack fell from 62% SOC to under-voltage trip after only ~4 Ah; upstream cause not separable in this data.
result.explanation: BMS under-voltage protection opened the contactors (how HV was lost). Why the cells were that low stays open: SOC drift, far lower usable capacity, or under-read current. The recording looks the same under all three.

evidence.quote: SHIFT battery.cell_voltage[min] changed level for good at t=619 s: median 3.2 before, 2.844 after V (7120x its variation before)
evidence.shows: Smooth pack-wide voltage decline at a constant 7.04 A load while SOC still read about 60%.
Level 3 fires with both contactors opening at the same time (lines 19-20), after levels 1 (t=1453) and 2 (t=1799). This is the protective response, not the origin.

evidence.quote: CHANGE battery.soc[bms] at t=2394.5 s: 57.6 -> 1.2 % (step -56.4, 47x its usual variation)
evidence.shows: SOC was corrected by 56 points only after the under-voltage trip, at rest. It had followed counted charge until then (charge_accounting PASS).

evidence.quote: CONSTANT battery.pack_current held 7.04 from t=0 to 2100 s (4201 samples)
evidence.shows: About 4.1 Ah was delivered against 62 Ah promised by the SOC. That means either ~58 pp SOC overstatement, ~6.6 Ah usable capacity, or ~15x current under-read.

After the SOC reset to 1.2%, HV was reclosed three times. Each time current flowed for ~12 s and the level went to 3 again. SOC stayed at 1.2 and the lowest cell dipped to 2.421 V, below the first trip.

checked.check: Sequence of departures from baseline, t=1190-2110
checked.result: Max cell voltage left baseline first (1233.5 s), then pack voltage (1354.5), min cell (1415.5), SOC (1869.0), current (2100.5, an effect of the opening). Fault level 1 at 1453, 2 at 1799, 3 at 2100.5.
checked.about: Under-voltage protection is a consequence; cell voltage drop is the earliest sign. Contactor-first order is not supported.

checked.check: Compare around the SOC reset, t=2394.5
checked.result: Only SOC changed (57.6 -> 1.2). Cell voltages were only settling (2.296 -> 2.282 V) and current was 0 before and after.
A, B and C are open and consistent with all the data. D (weak cell) is insufficient alone because the highest cell fell 450 mV against a 260 mV spread. E and F are weakened.
checked.about: Upstream cause: SOC, capacity or current sensing

checked.result: SOC frozen at 1.2% while 7.04 A flowed. The lowest cell fell to 2.421 V, below the 2.500 V original trip. Three reclosures each ended in level 3.
No similar closed cases in the workspace.

effects.why: Contactors opened at the same instant as level 3: BMS protective action.

effects.quote: CHANGE battery.pack_current at t=2094.5 s: 7.04 -> 0 A (step -7.04, 1000x its usual variation)
effects.why: Load ended when HV was lost, about 6 s before the recorded level 3 event (2100.5 s). The recording does not show who or what commanded it.

outcomes.label: All cells within a small spread
outcomes.means: Weak cell unlikely; the shortfall is pack-level (SOC, capacity or current sensing).
outcomes.then: Request BMS history, SOC algorithm docs and load inventory.

outcomes.label: Cell 24 far below the others
outcomes.means: A weak or imbalanced cell contributes and sets the early cutoff.
outcomes.then: Hand off to HV-qualified capacity test with all-cell logging.

outcomes.means: Over-discharge risk; no HV closure or charge until the manufacturer's recovery procedure is followed.

safety_findings.statement: Do not close HV or charge again until every cell's rest voltage is assessed; the lowest cell reached 2.421 V during reclosure, below the original trip level.
HV was reclosed three times after protective shutdowns and discharged deeper than the original trip. Needs review against the customer's restart policy, which is not available.
HV was closed 3 times after the protective shutdown at t=2100.5 s (3205.6, 3274.2, 3353.4 s). Whether this was permitted depends on a restart policy not available here.
Each of the 3 closures ended in another protective shutdown (3223.6, 3292.2, 3371.4 s): repeated trip cycles on a depleted pack. Needs engineering review.
The fault resets before each closure fall in a recording gap, so who or what reset the fault and why is not shown. Reset logic needs review.

unknowns: The data cannot separate SOC drift, low usable capacity and current under-read.
The protection thresholds and the restart-permission logic are not available.
The charge history before t=0 and the capacity parameter's origin are not available.
